concept_summary: Junos OS uses a hierarchical configuration structure with commit-based model where changes are staged before activation. Initial setup includes hostname, root authentication, management interface configuration, and system services. Configuration is done using 'set' commands that build a tree-structured configuration database. The candidate configuration must be committed to become active.
cli_mode_context: Enter configuration mode with 'configure' or 'edit' command from operational mode (>). Use 'set' commands to add configuration statements. Commit changes with 'commit' to activate them. Use 'show | display set' to view config as set commands.
example_commands:
configure
set system host-name mx-pe-router01
set system domain-name example.com
set system root-authentication plain-text-password
set system login user admin class super-user authentication plain-text-password
set interfaces fxp0 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.10/24
set system services ssh
set system services netconf ssh
set system syslog file messages any notice
set system syslog file messages authorization info
commit and-quit

key_parameters.description: Enters configuration mode (prompt changes from > to #)
Adds or modifies configuration statement in hierarchy
Activates candidate configuration (validates and applies changes)
Commits configuration and exits to operational mode

concept_summary: Junos interfaces use a hierarchical naming scheme with physical interface, logical unit, and protocol family levels. Physical interfaces are named by type and slot/port location. Logical units (subinterfaces) are numbered and support multiple protocol families (inet for IPv4, inet6 for IPv6). Interface configuration includes descriptions, encapsulation, and address family-specific parameters.
cli_mode_context: Configure interfaces under 'interfaces' hierarchy. Each interface has units (logical interfaces) which contain protocol families. Use 'set interfaces <name> unit <number> family <family>' structure.
example_commands:
configure
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 description "Core-Uplink-to-P-Router"
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.1/30
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet6 address 2001:db8::1/127
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 vlan-tagging
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 100 vlan-id 100
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 100 family inet address 198.51.100.1/24
set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.100/32
set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet6 address 2001:db8:ffff::1/128
commit

key_parameters.description: Physical interface (ge, xe, et for Ethernet; fxp for management)
Assigns VLAN ID to logical unit

concept_summary: Junos switches handle VLANs as Layer 2 broadcast domains associated with interfaces or interface ranges. VLAN configuration includes defining VLAN IDs, names, and Layer 3 interfaces (IRB - Integrated Routing and Bridging). Trunk ports carry multiple VLANs while access ports belong to single VLAN. Bridge domains provide advanced Layer 2 virtualization. RSTP or MSTP provide loop prevention.
cli_mode_context: Configure VLANs under 'vlans' hierarchy. Assign interfaces to VLANs under interface configuration. Use 'irb' interface for inter-VLAN routing. Configure switching protocols under 'protocols rstp' or 'protocols mstp'.
example_commands:
configure
set vlans engineering vlan-id 10
set vlans engineering l3-interface irb.10
set vlans sales vlan-id 20
set vlans sales l3-interface irb.20
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family ethernet-switching interface-mode access
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family ethernet-switching vlan members engineering
set interfaces ge-0/0/24 unit 0 family ethernet-switching interface-mode trunk
set interfaces ge-0/0/24 unit 0 family ethernet-switching vlan members [engineering sales]
set interfaces irb unit 10 family inet address 192.0.2.1/24
set interfaces irb unit 20 family inet address 198.51.100.1/24
set protocols rstp
commit

key_parameters.description: Creates VLAN with name and numeric ID (1-4094)
Associates VLAN with IRB interface for routing
Sets port as access port (single untagged VLAN)
Sets port as trunk port (multiple tagged VLANs)
Assigns interface to VLAN(s), use brackets for multiple
Integrated Routing and Bridging interface for inter-VLAN routing

concept_summary: Static routes provide explicit next-hop forwarding information for destination prefixes. Junos supports static routes with next-hop addresses, egress interfaces, or qualified next-hops with preferences. Static routes can be made conditional based on route reachability or installed into specific routing tables for multi-topology routing. Preference values determine route selection priority.
cli_mode_context: Configure static routes under 'routing-options static' hierarchy. Specify destination prefix and next-hop. Use 'preference' to adjust administrative distance. Use 'qualified-next-hop' for backup paths.
example_commands:
configure
set routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop 192.0.2.1
set routing-options static route 198.51.100.0/24 next-hop ge-0/0/1.0
set routing-options static route 203.0.113.0/24 next-hop 192.0.2.5
set routing-options static route 203.0.113.0/24 preference 10
set routing-options static route 203.0.113.0/24 qualified-next-hop 192.0.2.6 preference 20
set routing-options static route 203.0.113.128/25 discard
set routing-options rib inet6.0 static route ::/0 next-hop 2001:db8::1
commit

key_parameters.description: Defines static route with destination prefix
Specifies next-hop IP address or interface
Rejects traffic and sends ICMP unreachable
Prevents route from being advertised to routing protocols

concept_summary: OSPF in Junos is a link-state IGP supporting hierarchical area design and SPF computation. Configuration uses area-based structure with interfaces explicitly assigned to areas. Junos supports OSPFv2 for IPv4 and OSPFv3 for IPv6 with advanced features like graceful restart, BFD integration, and traffic engineering extensions. Reference bandwidth and interface costs determine path selection.
cli_mode_context: Configure OSPF under 'protocols ospf' for IPv4 or 'protocols ospfv3' for IPv6. Define areas and include interfaces within area configuration. Set router-id in routing-options.
example_commands:
configure
set routing-options router-id 192.0.2.1
set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface lo0.0 passive
set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/0.0 interface-type p2p
set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/0.0 metric 10
set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.10 interface ge-0/0/1.0
set protocols ospf reference-bandwidth 100g
set protocols ospf graceful-restart
set protocols ospfv3 area 0.0.0.0 interface lo0.0 passive
set protocols ospfv3 area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/0.0
commit

key_parameters.description: Suppresses OSPF hellos while advertising prefix

concept_summary: BGP in Junos is path-vector protocol for inter-domain routing with extensive policy control. Configuration uses group-based structure where neighbors inherit properties from groups. Junos supports multiple address families (inet, inet6, inet-vpn, evpn) and advanced features like route reflection, graceful restart, and add-path. Routing policies control route import and export using match/action logic.
cli_mode_context: Configure BGP under 'protocols bgp'. Define groups with type (internal or external), then add neighbors. Configure routing policies under 'policy-options' and apply with import/export statements.
example_commands:
configure
set routing-options autonomous-system 65001
set policy-options policy-statement ACCEPT-ALL then accept
set protocols bgp group EBGP-PEERS type external
set protocols bgp group EBGP-PEERS peer-as 65002
set protocols bgp group EBGP-PEERS neighbor 198.51.100.1 description ISP-Connection
set protocols bgp group EBGP-PEERS export ACCEPT-ALL
set protocols bgp group IBGP-PEERS type internal
set protocols bgp group IBGP-PEERS local-address 192.0.2.1
set protocols bgp group IBGP-PEERS neighbor 192.0.2.254
set protocols bgp group IBGP-PEERS family inet unicast
set protocols bgp group IBGP-PEERS family inet-vpn unicast
commit

key_parameters.description: Creates BGP peer group with name
Specifies neighbor AS (for EBGP or IBGP with different AS)
Source address for BGP sessions (recommended for IBGP)
Applies routing policy to outbound routes
Applies routing policy to inbound routes

concept_summary: IS-IS is a link-state IGP commonly used in service provider networks for its scalability and protocol independence. Junos implements IS-IS with support for both narrow and wide metrics, multi-topology routing, and traffic engineering. Configuration requires NET address and explicit interface assignment. IS-IS operates at Layer 2 making it independent of IP addressing. Level-1 and Level-2 routing provide hierarchical scalability.
cli_mode_context: Configure IS-IS under 'protocols isis'. Set NET address under 'routing-options router-id' and 'protocols isis'. Add interfaces to IS-IS explicitly. Configure level-1, level-2, or both.
example_commands:
configure
set protocols isis level 2 wide-metrics-only
set protocols isis interface lo0.0 level 2 passive
set protocols isis interface ge-0/0/0.0 point-to-point
set protocols isis interface ge-0/0/0.0 level 2 metric 10
set protocols isis interface ge-0/0/1.0 level 2 metric 10
set protocols isis net 49.0001.0192.0000.2001.00
set protocols isis reference-bandwidth 100g
set protocols isis family inet unicast
set protocols isis family inet6 unicast
commit

key_parameters.description: Suppresses IS-IS hellos while advertising prefix

concept_summary: VRRP in Junos provides first-hop redundancy with virtual IP addressing for gateway high availability. Multiple routers share virtual IP with one acting as master based on priority election. Junos supports VRRPv2 for IPv4 and VRRPv3 for IPv6 with features like authentication, preemption control, and interface tracking. VRRP operates at Layer 3 interface level with group numbering for multiple virtual routers.
cli_mode_context: Configure VRRP under interface family inet or inet6 hierarchy. Define virtual addresses and priority values. Enable preemption and tracking as needed.
example_commands:
configure
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.2/24 vrrp-group 1 virtual-address 192.0.2.1
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.2/24 vrrp-group 1 priority 110
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.2/24 vrrp-group 1 preempt
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.2/24 vrrp-group 1 accept-data
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.2/24 vrrp-group 1 authentication-type md5
set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.2/24 vrrp-group 1 authentication-key "$9$secret"
set interfaces ge-0/0/6 unit 0 family inet6 address 2001:db8:10::2/64 vrrp-inet6-group 1 virtual-inet6-address 2001:db8:10::1
set interfaces ge-0/0/6 unit 0 family inet6 address 2001:db8:10::2/64 vrrp-inet6-group 1 priority 110
commit

concept_summary: Junos uses firewall filters for packet filtering based on Layer 2-4 criteria. Filters contain terms with match conditions and actions (accept, discard, reject). Filters are applied to interfaces or routing instances in input or output direction. Stateless filters operate per-packet while stateful inspection is available through security zones. Filters support logging, counting, and policer actions.
cli_mode_context: Define filters under 'firewall family inet filter' for IPv4 or 'family inet6 filter' for IPv6. Each filter contains terms with match conditions and actions. Apply to interfaces with 'set interfaces <name> unit X family inet filter input/output'.
example_commands:
configure
set firewall family inet filter BLOCK-TELNET term deny-telnet from protocol tcp
set firewall family inet filter BLOCK-TELNET term deny-telnet from destination-port telnet
set firewall family inet filter BLOCK-TELNET term deny-telnet then log
set firewall family inet filter BLOCK-TELNET term deny-telnet then discard
set firewall family inet filter BLOCK-TELNET term allow-all then accept
set firewall family inet filter PERMIT-MGMT term allow-ssh from source-address 192.0.2.0/24
set firewall family inet filter PERMIT-MGMT term allow-ssh from protocol tcp
set firewall family inet filter PERMIT-MGMT term allow-ssh from destination-port ssh
set firewall family inet filter PERMIT-MGMT term allow-ssh then accept
set firewall family inet filter PERMIT-MGMT term deny-all then log
set firewall family inet filter PERMIT-MGMT term deny-all then discard
set interfaces ge-0/0/10 unit 0 family inet filter input BLOCK-TELNET
commit

concept_summary: Junos supports NAT for address translation in various deployment scenarios. Source NAT translates private addresses to public addresses with pool-based or interface-based mappings. Destination NAT redirects traffic to internal servers. Static NAT provides one-to-one mappings. NAT is configured within security zones on SRX platforms or using filters and service sets on MX routers. Port Address Translation extends address conservation.
cli_mode_context: For SRX series, configure NAT under 'security nat source' or 'security nat destination' with rules and pools. For MX series, use service filters with NAT next-hop-service. Define zones and policies as needed.
example_commands:
configure
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security nat source pool PUBLIC-POOL address 198.51.100.1/32 to 198.51.100.10/32
set security nat source rule-set INSIDE-TO-INTERNET from zone trust
set security nat source rule-set INSIDE-TO-INTERNET to zone untrust
set security nat source rule-set INSIDE-TO-INTERNET rule PAT-RULE match source-address 192.0.2.0/24
set security nat source rule-set INSIDE-TO-INTERNET rule PAT-RULE then source-nat pool PUBLIC-POOL
set security nat static rule-set STATIC-NAT from zone untrust
set security nat static rule-set STATIC-NAT rule SERVER-NAT match destination-address 198.51.100.50/32
set security nat static rule-set STATIC-NAT rule SERVER-NAT then static-nat prefix 192.0.2.10/32
commit

concept_summary: Junos supports IPsec VPNs for securing IP communications through encryption and authentication. Site-to-site VPNs use IKE for key negotiation and IPsec SA for data protection. Configuration includes IKE proposals and policies for phase 1, IPsec proposals and policies for phase 2, and VPN definitions binding peers with traffic selectors. Both route-based (st0 interfaces) and policy-based VPNs are supported.
cli_mode_context: Configure IPsec VPN under 'security ike' and 'security ipsec'. Define proposals, policies, and VPN bindings. For route-based VPN, configure st0 tunnel interface. Apply security policies permitting traffic.

set security ike proposal IKE-PROP authentication-method pre-shared-keys

set security ipsec proposal IPSEC-PROP protocol esp

set security ipsec proposal IPSEC-PROP authentication-algorithm hmac-sha-256-128
set security ipsec policy IPSEC-POLICY proposals IPSEC-PROP

set security ipsec vpn SITE-TO-SITE-VPN ike ipsec-policy IPSEC-POLICY

set security zones security-zone vpn interfaces st0.0

concept_summary: Junos QoS uses classifiers to assign traffic to forwarding classes and loss priorities. Schedulers define bandwidth allocation, priority, and drop profiles. Rewrite rules mark outgoing packets with DSCP or CoS values. BA (Behavior Aggregate) classifiers use existing markings while MF (Multi-Field) classifiers use firewall filters. Hierarchical scheduling supports complex traffic management with queues and shapers.
cli_mode_context: Define classifiers under 'class-of-service', create schedulers and scheduler-maps, configure rewrite rules, and apply to interfaces. Use firewall filters for classification and policers for rate limiting.
example_commands:
configure
set class-of-service classifiers dscp DSCP-CLASSIFIER forwarding-class expedited-forwarding loss-priority low code-points ef
set class-of-service classifiers dscp DSCP-CLASSIFIER forwarding-class assured-forwarding loss-priority low code-points af31
set class-of-service forwarding-classes class expedited-forwarding queue-num 0

set class-of-service schedulers DATA-SCHED transmit-rate percent 50
set class-of-service scheduler-maps CORE-OUT forwarding-class expedited-forwarding scheduler VOICE-SCHED

set class-of-service interfaces ge-0/0/0 scheduler-map CORE-OUT
set class-of-service interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 classifiers dscp DSCP-CLASSIFIER
commit

concept_summary: Junos AAA provides centralized authentication and authorization using RADIUS or TACACS+ servers with local fallback. User classes define privilege levels and command authorization. Login classes determine shell access and permissions. Authentication order defines server precedence with local accounts as backup. Junos supports per-user and per-class authorization with granular command control.
cli_mode_context: Configure AAA under 'system' hierarchy. Define RADIUS or TACACS+ servers, create login classes, configure authentication order, and assign users to classes.
example_commands:

set system tacplus-server 192.0.2.50 secret "$9$TacacsSecret"
set system tacplus-server 192.0.2.50 source-address 192.0.2.100
set system tacplus-server 192.0.2.51 secret "$9$TacacsSecret"
set system authentication-order [tacplus password]
set system accounting events login
set system accounting events change-log
set system accounting destination tacplus
set system login class operator permissions [clear network reset trace view]
set system login class operator allow-commands "show"
set system login class operator deny-commands "(clear|request)"
set system login user netops class operator
set system login user netops authentication encrypted-password "$6$hash"
set system login user admin class super-user

concept_summary: Junos supports SNMP v1, v2c, and v3 for network monitoring with MIB access and trap generation. SNMPv3 provides authentication and encryption. Logging supports multiple destinations with severity filtering including console, files, and remote syslog servers. Structured logging provides machine-parseable output. NETCONF and JTI (Junos Telemetry Interface) offer modern data collection methods.

concept_summary: Junos provides comprehensive EVPN-VXLAN support for data center fabrics and overlay networks. EVPN uses BGP for control plane to distribute MAC/IP information while VXLAN provides UDP-based encapsulation for overlay tunneling. Junos supports EVPN Type-2 for MAC/IP routes, Type-3 for inclusive multicast, and Type-5 for IP prefix routes. ESI (Ethernet Segment Identifier) enables multihoming with active-active forwarding.

concept_summary: Junos provides high availability through redundant hardware and software features. Chassis cluster creates active-passive or active-active pairs with synchronized state. GRES (Graceful Routing Engine Switchover) maintains protocol state during RE failover. NSR (Nonstop Active Routing) keeps protocol sessions active. Graceful restart protocols minimize disruption during control plane failures. Virtual Chassis stacks multiple switches into single logical device.

concept_summary: Junos system management includes configuration commit system with rollback capability, software installation and upgrade procedures, configuration archival, and rescue configuration. Configurations are versioned with numbered commits allowing precise rollback. Software upgrades use unified package installation with atomic activation. Rescue configuration provides emergency recovery path. Configuration can be archived to remote servers automatically or on-demand.
cli_mode_context: Use 'commit' to activate configuration with optional comments. Use 'rollback' to revert to previous config. Use 'request system software add' for upgrades. Configure archival under 'system archival configuration'.
example_commands:
configure
set system archival configuration transfer-on-commit
set system archival configuration archive-sites ftp://192.0.2.50/configs/
commit comment "Initial production configuration"
commit confirmed 5
commit and-quit
exit
show system commit
show system rollback compare 0 1
configure
rollback 1
commit
request system configuration rescue save
request system software add /var/tmp/junos-install-mx-x86-64-23.2R1.14.tgz reboot
show system software
request system snapshot slice alternate
